Copilot Studio product
Copilot Studio is a Microsoft product for building and customizing AI-powered assistants and workflows.
core banking systems concept
Core banking systems are the main computer systems banks use to manage accounts, payments, loans, and customer records.
core_pattern concept
core_pattern is a Linux kernel setting that controls where crash dump files are saved or what program handles them.
corporate banking records concept
Corporate banking records are business financial documents such as account information, transactions, loans, and payment history.
corporate networks concept
Corporate networks are the connected computers, servers, and systems used by a company.
covered entities organization
Covered entities are healthcare organizations, plans, or clearinghouses that must follow HIPAA privacy and security rules.
covert access concept
Covert access is hidden or stealthy access to a system that the owner is not meant to notice.
Credential interception technique
Credential interception is stealing usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login secrets while they are being entered or transmitted.
credential rotation technique
Credential rotation means replacing passwords, keys, or tokens with new ones to reduce the risk from stolen or old credentials.
credential stealer malware
A credential stealer is malware designed to steal usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential theft technique
Credential theft is the stealing of usernames, passwords, tokens, or other login information.
credential-harvesting
Credential harvesting is collecting usernames, passwords, or login tokens from victims.
credentials concept
Credentials are login details or access tokens that prove a user or system is allowed to access something.
Credit card numbers concept
Credit card numbers are payment card identifiers that criminals try to steal for fraud.
critical infrastructure concept
Critical infrastructure refers to essential systems and services that societies and organizations depend on.
critical infrastructure operators organization
Critical infrastructure operators are organizations that run essential services such as power, water, transport, or communications.
Critical services concept
Critical services are essential systems or functions whose failure would seriously harm operations or public services.
critical systems concept
Critical systems are important systems whose failure could seriously affect operations or safety.
Critical vulnerability vulnerability
A critical vulnerability is a very serious security flaw that can cause major damage if exploited.
cron tool
cron is a Unix tool that runs scheduled commands or scripts automatically at set times.
cron-related paths concept
Cron-related paths are file or folder locations used by the cron scheduler to run tasks automatically on Unix-like systems.
cross-account trust concept
Cross-account trust lets an identity or service in one account access resources or roles in another account.
CRSBench tool
CRSBench is a benchmark or evaluation tool referenced in security reporting.
CryptanalysisBench tool
CryptanalysisBench is a named benchmarking tool or dataset referenced in cryptography or security research.
CSRF technique
CSRF is a web attack where a site is tricked into performing an action using a logged-in user's session without the user's intent.
CubePilot organization
CubePilot is a company or project known for autopilot and navigation hardware used in drones and robotic systems.
cubepilot.org organization
cubepilot.org is a website domain associated with CubePilot, a maker of autopilot and drone navigation hardware.
curl
curl is a command-line tool used to transfer data to or from servers using protocols like HTTP and HTTPS.
cursor
Cursor is an AI-assisted code editor built for software developers.
Custom multi-stage malware malware
Custom multi-stage malware is attacker-made malicious software that runs in several steps, often downloading or unpacking later parts after it starts.
customer data concept
Customer data is information a company keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, or purchase history.
customer information concept
Customer information is data a business keeps about its customers, such as names, contact details, purchases, or account records.
CVE vulnerability
A CVE is a public identifier used to track a specific known software vulnerability.
CVE records concept
CVE records are public entries that identify and describe known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVEBench tool
CVEBench is a benchmark or evaluation tool that uses CVE-style vulnerability tasks to test security capabilities.
CVEs concept
CVEs are standardized public identifiers for known cybersecurity vulnerabilities.
CVSS score concept
A CVSS score is a standard number used to show how severe a software vulnerability is.
cyber concept
Cyber is a broad shorthand for things related to computers, networks, and digital security.
cyber espionage operations technique
Cyber espionage operations are hacking campaigns aimed at secretly stealing information for intelligence or strategic advantage.
cyber incident concept
A cyber incident is any event where digital systems, accounts, or data may have been attacked, exposed, or disrupted.
cyber incidents concept
Cyber incidents are events that threaten or harm computer systems, networks, or data.
Cyber-capability tests concept
Cyber-capability tests are evaluations that measure whether a system or person can perform cybersecurity tasks or attacks.
Cyber-Espionage concept
Cyber-espionage is spying through computers and networks to steal secrets or sensitive information.
cyberattack concept
A cyberattack is an attempt to damage, disrupt, or gain unauthorized access to computer systems or data.
cyberattacks concept
Malicious activities conducted over computer networks to steal data, disrupt operations, or damage systems.
CyberGym product
CyberGym is a cybersecurity evaluation or training platform referenced in security reporting.
CyberGym's public leaderboard product
CyberGym's public leaderboard is a ranking page that publicly compares results from CyberGym tasks or evaluations.
CyberSecEval4 product
CyberSecEval4 is a cybersecurity evaluation benchmark for testing AI systems on security-related tasks.
Cybersecurity concept
Cybersecurity is the practice of protecting computers, networks, software, and data from digital attacks or misuse.
cybersecurity incident concept
A cybersecurity incident is an event that threatens the security of systems, networks, or data.
cybersecurity researchers organization
Cybersecurity researchers are people who study digital threats, software flaws, and attacks to help protect systems.
Cyera organization
Cyera is a cybersecurity company focused on discovering and protecting sensitive data across cloud and enterprise systems.
Cypher tool
Cypher is a query language commonly used with graph databases such as Neo4j.
dark web activity concept
Dark web activity refers to actions on hidden parts of the internet, including forums and markets that may be used for cybercrime.
darknet forum concept
A darknet forum is an online discussion site on hidden networks where criminals may trade stolen data, tools, or services.
darknet marketplace concept
A darknet marketplace is a hidden online market where people may buy and sell illegal goods, stolen data, or hacking services.
data breach concept
A data breach is an incident where sensitive, private, or protected information is accessed, exposed, or stolen without permission.
data exfiltration technique
Data exfiltration is the unauthorized removal or copying of data from a system.
data exposure concept
Data exposure means sensitive information is left accessible to people or systems that should not be able to see it.
data leakage concept
Data leakage is when sensitive information is exposed or shared outside where it should be, accidentally or maliciously.
data security concept
Data security is the practice of protecting information from unauthorized access, theft, damage, or exposure.
data theft concept
Data theft is the stealing of information from a system or service.
datasets concept
Datasets are collections of information that researchers or tools analyze to find patterns and evidence.
Dates of birth concept
Dates of birth are personal information that can help identify someone and may be sensitive if exposed.
DDoS technique
DDoS is an attack that floods a website or service with traffic from many sources so legitimate users cannot access it.
Debian product
A well-known community-driven Linux distribution famous for its stability and package management system.
Debug technique
Debug means to inspect software or systems to find and fix errors, and attackers can sometimes abuse debugging features to learn how something works.
default credentials concept
Default credentials are factory-set usernames and passwords that should be changed because attackers often know them.
Default passwords concept
Default passwords are factory-set passwords that should be changed because attackers often know them.
defenders concept
Defenders are the people or teams responsible for protecting systems and responding to cyber threats.
Defensive security concept
Defensive security is the work of protecting systems, detecting attacks, and reducing the damage from cyber threats.
Dell organization
A major technology company known for personal computers, servers, and IT equipment.
dependencies concept
Dependencies are outside software components or libraries that an application needs in order to work.
dependency concept
A dependency is outside software that an application relies on, which can create risk if that outside component is vulnerable or malicious.
deserialization technique
The process of converting data from a stored format back into a runtime object, a common target for injection attacks.
detached Node.js process technique
A detached Node.js process is a JavaScript program started so it can keep running independently after the parent process exits.
detection concept
Detection is the process of finding signs of suspicious or malicious activity.
DEV#POPPER threat-actor

Developer credentials concept
Developer credentials are usernames, passwords, keys, or tokens that let someone access software development systems such as code repositories or build servers.
Developer machines concept
Developer machines are computers used by software developers to write, build, and test code.

DHCPv6 is the protocol that automatically gives IPv6 network configuration details to devices.

DHCPv6 REQUEST is a message a device sends to ask a DHCPv6 server to assign or confirm IPv6 configuration.
Diagnosis information concept
Diagnosis information is medical data about what condition, illness, or injury a person has been found to have.
Director of National Intelligence organization
The Director of National Intelligence is the U.S. official who oversees and coordinates the country’s intelligence agencies.
also: DNI, top intelligence official
directory listing concept
Directory listing is when a web server shows the files inside a folder, which can accidentally expose sensitive files.
Disclosure concept
Disclosure is the act of reporting or publishing information about a security issue so it can be understood and fixed.
Disconnect product
Disconnect is likely a product, command, or feature name referenced in a security or privacy context.
discord product
Discord is a communication platform for text, voice, and video chats, popular with gaming and online communities.
Discovery technique
Discovery is the attacker activity of learning about a victim’s systems, accounts, and network before taking further action.
disruption concept
Disruption is an interruption that prevents systems, services, or operations from working normally.
Distributed denial-of-service technique
A distributed denial-of-service attack floods a website or service with traffic from many sources so legitimate users cannot reach it.

DKIM is an email signing method that helps verify that a message was authorized by a domain and was not changed after signing.

DLL search-order hijacking is an attack where a program is tricked into loading a malicious DLL instead of the legitimate one it expected.

DLL side-loading is when attackers trick a legitimate program into loading a malicious DLL file.

DLP, or data loss prevention, is technology that helps stop sensitive information from being leaked or sent where it should not go.

DNS settings control which servers a device uses to translate website names into internet addresses.
dns-hijacking technique
DNS-hijacking is an attack that changes domain-name lookups so users are sent to the wrong or malicious destination.
Documentation portal product
A documentation portal is a website where users can read product manuals, setup guides, and technical reference material.
DOCX concept
DOCX is the modern Microsoft Word document file format, which can contain text, images, links, and sometimes risky embedded content.
Donald Trump other
Donald Trump is a U.S. political figure and former president.
also: Trump
Downstream policy violations concept
Downstream policy violations are rule-breaking actions that happen later in a workflow, after data or requests have moved to another system or service.
downstream services concept
Downstream services are systems that receive data, requests, or dependencies from another service earlier in a workflow.
dropper malware
A dropper is malware whose main job is to install or unpack other malware onto a device.
dynamic imports technique
Dynamic imports are a programming feature that loads code only when it is needed, which can affect security if the loaded source is untrusted.
EC2 product
Amazon EC2 is Amazon Web Services’ cloud service for renting virtual servers.
Egidio Romano other
Egidio Romano is a named person referenced in security reporting, likely as a researcher, developer, or public figure.
EKS product
EKS, or Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service, is AWS's managed service for running Kubernetes clusters.
election interference concept
Election interference is an attempt to influence, disrupt, or undermine an election through illegal, deceptive, or covert means.
ELF concept
ELF is a common executable file format used by Linux and other Unix-like operating systems.
email account concept
An email account is a user's mailbox and login identity for sending and receiving email.

Email account compromise happens when an attacker gains access to someone’s email account and can read or send messages as that person.
email authentication concept
Technical methods that verify an email came from the domain it claims and hasn't been forged.
embedded connections concept
Embedded connections are stored links or credentials inside an app or workflow that let it connect to other services.
employee's email account concept
An employee's email account is a work mailbox that attackers may target to steal messages, reset passwords, or impersonate the employee.
empty username concept
An empty username is a login attempt where the username field is blank, which can matter if a system mishandles authentication.
encrypted concept
Encrypted data has been scrambled so that only someone with the right key can read it.
encryption concept
Encryption is a way of scrambling information so only someone with the right key can read it.
end to end concept
End to end means something is handled across the whole process from start to finish, often without gaps between steps.
endpoint concept
An endpoint is a user device such as a laptop, phone, or server that connects to a network.
endpoints concept
Endpoints are user-facing devices such as laptops, desktops, or phones that connect to systems and data.

Enterprise environments are the large, managed technology systems used by organizations rather than individual home users.

Microsoft Entra is Microsoft’s identity and access management product family, including cloud directory and login services.

The Entra Agents extension is a Microsoft Entra-related component that adds agent capabilities or integrations.
entra-id

entry points concept
Entry points are the places where attackers can first get into a system or network.
Enumeration technique
Enumeration is the process of systematically listing users, files, services, or other details about a system.
ERP portal product
An ERP portal is a web interface for accessing enterprise resource planning systems that manage business functions like finance, inventory, and HR.
escalated privileges technique
Escalated privileges mean gaining more powerful permissions than a user or attacker originally had.
escaping technique
Escaping means changing special characters in text so a computer treats them as normal text instead of as commands or code.
espionage concept
Espionage is spying to gather information without permission.

The EU AI Act is a European Union law that sets rules for artificial intelligence systems based on their risks.
european-union
The European Union is a political and economic union of European countries that also creates cybersecurity and privacy rules.

eval() is a programming function that runs text as code, which can be dangerous if attackers control the text.

Execute code means to make a computer run instructions, which is dangerous if an attacker can run their own code.

Execution is the stage where an attacker runs code or commands on a target system.

Execution vectors are the ways attackers or software can cause code or commands to run on a system.
also: execution vector
Exfiltrate sensitive data technique
To exfiltrate sensitive data means to secretly steal and move private information out of a system or organization.
exfiltrated technique
Exfiltrated means data was secretly copied or moved out of a system by an attacker.
exploit technique
An exploit is code or a method that takes advantage of a security flaw to make something happen that should not be allowed.
exploit code tool
Exploit code is software written to take advantage of a security flaw in a system or application.
exploitation technique
Exploitation is taking advantage of a weakness in software or people to gain unauthorized access or control.
exploitation attempts technique
Exploitation attempts are tries to take advantage of a software weakness to gain access, run code, or cause harm.

Exploitation in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just testing it in a lab.
exploited in the wild concept
Exploited in the wild means attackers are actively using a vulnerability against real targets, not just in a lab.

ExploitGym is a cybersecurity evaluation tool or benchmark environment used to test how AI systems handle exploit-related tasks.

Exploits are code or techniques that take advantage of software vulnerabilities.
exposed credentials concept
Login details that have been accidentally published or stolen, granting unauthorized access.

Exposure hygiene means regularly finding and reducing the systems, accounts, and data that are visible or reachable by attackers.
external attack surface concept
An external attack surface is everything an organization exposes to the internet that attackers could try to target.

fallback concept
A fallback is a backup option used when the preferred option is unavailable or fails.
false positive concept
An alert that mistakenly flags benign activity as malicious, causing unnecessary work and potentially distracting from real threats.

Fastjson is a Java library from Alibaba used to read and write JSON data, and it has been involved in several security issues.
fbi organization

federal agencies organization
Federal agencies are government organizations that operate at the national level.

file operations concept
File operations are actions such as creating, changing, or deleting files.
file transfer concept
File transfer means moving a file from one computer, system, or user to another.

File-system timestamps are records showing when files were created, modified, or accessed.
financial information concept
Financial information is data about money, payments, bank accounts, cards, or transactions.

financial sector concept
The financial sector includes organizations and services involved in money, banking, investments, and payments.

flaw concept

frontier models concept

germany
Germany is a European country often referenced in cybersecurity reporting as a target, regulator, or law-enforcement partner.

google-accounts product

GPT-5.4 product

GPT-5.4-mini is a named compact version of a GPT artificial intelligence model referenced in AI reporting.
GPT-5.6 Sol product
GPT-5.6 Sol is a named AI model or model variant referenced in security reporting.

graph queries technique

grpc

guardrails concept

hackers concept
Individuals who use technical skills to gain unauthorized access to computer systems, or security researchers who test defenses.
hacking group concept

HAWK-512 protocol
HAWK-512 is a specific parameter set of the HAWK post-quantum digital signature scheme, referenced in cryptography research.
headers concept

healthcare organizations organization
Healthcare organizations are groups that provide, support, or manage healthcare services.
healthcare providers organization

A helpdesk is a support team that helps users with account, computer, and access problems.

hostname concept

Hugging Face organization
Hugging Face is a company and platform for sharing machine learning models, datasets, and AI tools.
human resources organization

incident response concept

incidents concept

india

Indicators of Compromise are clues such as addresses, file names, or patterns that can show malicious activity happened.

init scripts concept

injection technique

integrity concept

internal emails concept

investigation concept

Production classifiers tool

production database concept

production systems concept
Production systems are the real live systems an organization uses to run its services or business.
Project Perception product
Project Perception is a named project referenced in security reporting.
Prompt concept

prompts concept
Prompts are the instructions or questions a user gives to an AI system to get a response.
proof-of-concept technique

Proof-of-concept code is sample code that shows a security flaw can be exploited, often used by researchers and sometimes copied by attackers.
proof-of-concept exploit concept
A proof-of-concept exploit is sample code or a demonstration showing that a vulnerability can really be used.

Protobuf is a Google-made format for packaging structured data so programs can exchange it efficiently.
proxies tool

proxy concept
A proxy is an intermediate server that forwards internet traffic between a user and a destination.
public blockchain transaction concept
A public blockchain transaction is a record of activity on a blockchain that anyone can view and verify.
public dictionaries tool

ransom note concept

reachability concept

real-world attacks concept

recommendation concept

reconnaissance technique

red teamers concept

redirect concept

relay concept

remediate concept

remediated concept

remote access concept

remote access trojan malware

remote attacker concept

remote attackers concept

repository concept

researchers organization

resource control policies concept

REST API protocol

Restart concept

review process concept
A review process is the set of steps people use to examine and approve work before it is accepted.
RFQ concept
RFQ usually means Request for Quotation, a business document asking suppliers to provide pricing.

routers product

runMaths() tool

runtime concept

russia

Rust 1.98 is a specific version of the Rust programming language toolchain.

safeguards concept

scanning technique
